title: partials: centre atom, rho(z) and rho(r)
purpose: Exercises the three restricted modes of `partials` [@epsrmanual]: the g(r) of all atom types around one centre type (`atom-c`), the density profile along z about a centre type (`atom-z`) and the density versus distance in the xy-plane about a centre type (`atom-r`), together with the no-accumulation branch (`nsumt -1`) and the range scaling `rnormalise`.
system: Analysed configuration: `200DMSO400Water.ato`, an unchanged copy of the EPSR-test box of 200 dimethyl sulphoxide (DMSO; atom types S, O, C, H) and 400 water molecules (O1, H1): 3200 atoms, DMSO mole fraction 1/3, 300 K, cubic box of side 33.1213 Å (0.0881 atoms/Å³), the EPSR model of the deuterated DMSO-water neutron data (ISIS SANDALS runs SLS03863, SLS03871, SLS03850), cf. [@soperluzar1992]. `centreO1`: the 6 g(r) of every type around water O1, normalised with the O1 density, 200 points out to 0.8 of the default range; `rhozS`: number density versus the z separation from DMSO S atoms, 150 points; `rhorO`: number density versus the distance in the xy-plane from DMSO O atoms, 100 points over half the default range (`rnormalise 0.5`). Such profiles characterise the local environment of one site [@hansenmcdonald2006].
inputs: Three keyword files: `centreO1.PARTIALS.dat` (`atom-c O1`, `nz 200`, `rnormalise 0.8`, `nsumt -1`), `rhozS.PARTIALS.dat` (`atom-z S`, `nz 150`, `nsumt 0`), `rhorO.PARTIALS.dat` (`atom-r O`, `nz 100`, `rnormalise 0.5`, `nsumt 0`); `200DMSO400Water.ato` copied unchanged from EPSR-test.
verification: `commands.txt` runs the three inputs in sequence and the whole list twice. `centreO1` (`nsumt -1`) writes the single-configuration result in both passes and its `nsumt` stays -1; `rhozS` and `rhorO` accumulate (reference after pass 2: `nsumt 2`). Compared: the three `.PARTIALS.g01` files, the three rewritten `.dat` files and `fort.14`, which every run overwrites, so the one of `rhorO` is kept: it lists only the 6 pairs O-S ... O-H1 with O as centre.
notes: `fort.14`: the Fortran writes these lines to unit 14 after `save_files_others` has closed it, so gfortran creates the default file `fort.14`; the port writes the same file.
